answers: San Francisco-area cops have arrested three more young men in the savage gang rape, beating, and robbery of a 15-year-old girl outside her homecoming dance while dozens more watched. Five youths are being held, ranging from a 15-year-old boy who knew the victim to a 21-year-old. The girl was drinking outside the dance Saturday night, reports the San Francisco Chronicle, and the group turned on her when she became drunk. Charges are expected today. "This was a barbaric act. I still cannot get my head around the fact that numerous people either watched, walked away or participated in her assault," a Richmond cop tells the AP. "It's one of the most disturbing crimes in my 15 years as a police officer." Some students began transferring out of the school. "It's not safe there at all," said a 16-year-old girl. "I'm not going back."

The assault lasted for over two hours, and as many as two dozen people reportedly witnessed the attack without intervening or notifying authorities.

Two suspects were initially arrested, including Manuel Ortega, a 19-year-old former student who was apprehended as he tried to flee the scene. Ortega was charged with rape, robbery, and kidnapping. A 15-year-old student, who knew the victim, was also arrested and booked on suspicion of sexual assault. Police later expanded their list of suspects, indicating that up to 10 individuals, ranging in age from 15 to their early 20s, were involved in the attack. The assailants reportedly laughed and took photos during the assault.

The victim was found semiconscious and naked from the waist down near a picnic table and was airlifted to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Police are offering a $20,000 reward for information leading to the conviction of any of the assailants and are preparing for additional arrests. The case has sparked outrage and raised concerns about campus security, as Richmond High School, which has experienced a series of violent incidents, is currently without functioning surveillance cameras despite having approved a new system.

Richmond, a city known for its high crime rate, has seen a spike in homicides, with 44 killings reported so far in 2009. The attack has further shaken the community, prompting some students to leave the school. The incident has also drawn criticism of the school's security measures, as only four police officers and several security staff were present during the dance, with two site supervisors leaving early due to a prior commitment. The case has been described as one of the most disturbing crimes in the area, with law enforcement officials expressing deep concern over the lack of intervention from witnesses and the disturbing nature of the attack.
